title: Strategy (behavioral)
points: Put each variation of an algorithm in its own class behind a shared interface and inject the one to use.
Replaces if/else or switch chains with polymorphism. The caller calls the same method; the injected class decides how.
Answers: how should I do this thing?
trade: OCP in practice: new behaviour is a new class. Easy to test each alone. Not worth it for two fixed branches (KISS). Strategy vs State: a strategy is chosen from outside and doesn't change itself; states switch each other.
test: A method has an if/else chain on payment type. How do you refactor it with Strategy, and which SOLID principle does it satisfy?
answer: One class per payment type behind a PaymentStrategy interface, injected into the caller. This satisfies OCP: a new type is a new class.

questions.question: A method has a long if/else on payment type, and you add a branch for each new type. Which pattern removes the chain?
questions.explanation: Strategy: one class per variant behind an interface, injected into the caller. A new type is a new class, which is OCP.

questions.question: Strategy vs State: what is the key difference?
options: Strategy is chosen from outside and doesn't change itself; State objects switch to the next state
State uses interfaces, Strategy uses abstract classes
Strategy is creational, State is structural
questions.explanation: Both swap behaviour via an object. A strategy is injected and stays, while states represent a lifecycle and return the next state.
